text.title: 代表水的小球
text.situation:
低桌上的彩色球代表原子。乔把两个氢球接到一个氧球上，拼出水分子模型。分子模型比真实分子大得多，讲解员提醒游客不要按模型比例想象实物。后面的板把气体列为物质状态之一。卡片分别标出氧气和氢气，原子图展示一个原子的结构。玛雅一手拿完整水模型，一手拿一个球；两者回答同一种物质的不同问题。

乔：这个球是分子吗？
讲解员：这里它代表原子，连接成组的球代表分子。
玛雅：这些颜色是真实的吗？
讲解员：颜色帮助区分模型部件，真实原子不是这些涂色球。

paragraphs.en: On a low table, coloured balls represented atoms. Jo joined two hydrogen balls to one oxygen ball to build the model of a water molecule. The molecular model was much larger than any real molecule, and the guide asked visitors not to take its scale literally. Behind it, a board named gas as one state of matter. Separate cards identified oxygen and hydrogen gases, while an atomic diagram showed the structure of one atom. Maya kept the whole water model in one hand and an individual ball in the other. The two objects answered different questions about the same material.

paragraphs.en:
Jo: Is this ball a molecule?
Guide: Here it represents an atom. The joined group represents a molecule.
Maya: Are the colours real?
Guide: They help us distinguish the model parts; real atoms are not these painted balls.
